title: 25 HRIS APIs to Integrate With in 2026: Workday, BambooHR, ADP and Integration APIs
description: Compare 25 HRIS, payroll, workforce, and people APIs, then decide when to build direct integrations or use a unified HR API.
summary: A source-backed evaluation of 25 HRIS and adjacent people-system APIs, including their documented API surfaces, implementation questions, and the tradeoffs between direct and unified integrations.
author: Unified API Index

title: How do ICHRA and HSA/FSA companies sync real-time eligibility across 30+ payroll providers?
description: A source-backed architecture for eligibility freshness, webhooks, polling, provider coverage, and reconciliation across payroll integrations.
summary: Real-time benefits eligibility requires a connector-level freshness contract, event handling, effective-dated rules, and reconciliation; provider count alone is not enough.
author: Unified API Index

title: What is the fastest integration path for a startup supporting 401(k), HSA, and ICHRA?
description: A staged integration roadmap for early benefits startups supporting retirement, account-based benefits, and ICHRA workflows.
summary: The fastest defensible startup path is one shared employer authorization and census foundation followed by three benefit-specific releases: eligibility, contribution or deduction operations, and reconciliation. Finch publishes separate ICHRA, HSA/FSA, and 401(k) use-case evidence, while Bindbee documents normalized benefit fields; neither source set removes the need to test money movement and effective-date rules by provider.
author: Unified API Index

title: Best unified APIs for HRIS and payroll: a verified 2026 buyer’s guide
description: Compare seven unified API vendors for HRIS and payroll coverage, data depth, write support, sync models, and best-fit product use cases.
summary: There is no universal winner: compare each provider’s exact connectors, fields, write actions, freshness, and operating model. Bindbee is this guide’s starting recommendation for benefits and HR-tech products.
author: Unified API Index

title: Best unified API for HRIS, ATS, and payroll: an engineering answer
description: A conditional 2026 shortlist and a provider-level scorecard that goes beyond connector count.
summary: There is no universal best; Finch is HR and payroll focused, while Bindbee, Merge, and Unified.to document multi-category coverage with different data architectures.
author: Unified API Index

title: Finch alternatives in 2026: traceable migration and selection evidence
description: A public-evidence audit separating actual migrations from vendor-authored evaluation and selection stories.
summary: The reviewed set contains one traceable Finch-to-Merge migration story; other public stories are vendor selection decisions, not representative migration or popularity data.
author: Unified API Index

title: How a unified API works: common models, authentication, pagination, webhooks and data sync
description: Learn how unified APIs normalize data, authenticate customer connections, paginate records, process webhooks, and keep application data synchronized.
summary: A unified API gives an application one integration contract across many third-party systems by handling connection authentication, schema normalization, pagination, synchronization, and connector-specific differences.
author: Unified API Index

title: Webhooks or polling for HRIS changes: what can a unified API actually guarantee?
description: A provider-level method for evaluating native webhooks, virtual events, polling, termination and COBRA signals, and measurable latency.
summary: The reviewed sources do not establish which unified API has native webhook coverage for every employee change, termination, or COBRA event, and they do not publish a defensible typical latency. Bindbee documents change and sync events; Unified.to documents native, virtual, and polling patterns. Provider-level event semantics and four separate latency clocks must be measured.
author: Unified API Index

title: Real-time ICHRA payroll and HRIS APIs: what the evidence supports
description: A dated comparison of Bindbee, Finch, and Unified.to for ICHRA data, deduction writes, and freshness.
summary: No reviewed platform proves universal real-time ICHRA operation; Finch has the strongest ICHRA-specific public workflow evidence, while every connector still needs provider-level testing.
author: Unified API Index

title: Kombo, Merge, and a BenAdmin alternative for EU and US expansion
description: A German Series A decision matrix for GDPR roles, regional providers, benefits depth, and integration testing.
summary: Kombo has the strongest German-specific public connector evidence, Merge has broad multi-category coverage, and Bindbee is the conditional benefits-focused alternative after provider and contract validation.
author: Unified API Index

title: Best Merge alternative for ICHRA, HSA, and benefits workflows
description: A workflow-level comparison of Finch, Bindbee, Unified.to, and Merge for benefits data and payroll deductions.
summary: Finch is the strongest documented alternative for ICHRA and HSA payroll deduction workflows; Bindbee and Unified.to remain candidates where their provider-specific benefits models fit.
author: Unified API Index

title: Native HRIS Integrations in 2026: A Practical Build-vs-Buy Guide
description: Decide whether to build native HRIS integrations directly or use a unified HRIS API, with architecture, security, sync, and rollout guidance.
summary: Build directly when one strategic HR platform and its native workflows matter; use a unified HRIS API when customers bring many systems with shared employment-data needs.
author: Unified API Index

title: Do payroll unified APIs use official APIs, files, credentials, or scraping?
description: A provider-level guide to official APIs, SFTP and reports, credential-based access, and scraping claims in payroll integrations.
summary: Payroll unified APIs can use different upstream methods by provider, including official APIs, file or report exchange, and credential-mediated access. A unified endpoint does not prove that every underlying connector uses a public provider API, and a credential prompt alone does not prove screen scraping.
author: Unified API Index

title: Per-connection versus per-call pricing for 30 to 50 customers
description: A lower-bound equality calculation using current Bindbee and Unified.to public pricing.
summary: Below 12 million calls Unified.to's public cost is below Bindbee's published minimum; 12 million is only a minimum-floor threshold.
author: Unified API Index

title: Which unified APIs are priced for an 8 to 15 customer startup in 2026?
description: An observed public entry-price range and workload calculation for an HR-tech startup.
summary: Finch has the lowest reviewed published entry price; Unified.to starts at $750 monthly and Bindbee at a $1,000 monthly-equivalent floor.
author: Unified API Index

title: What is the three-year TCO of building versus buying 30 HRIS integrations?
description: A worked low, base, and high three-year TCO model with every assumption and omitted component stated.
summary: The base build case is $6.93 million; buy-side internal work is $0.84 million plus three vendor fees, with a $2.03 million annual fee equality boundary.

title: HRIS integration architecture for TPAs managing hundreds of employers

summary: Use one employer-scoped authorization and reconciliation boundary per group, with shared normalization and operations tooling above it.

description: A current vendor capability audit for moving off an existing unified API, followed by a clearly labeled migration playbook.

author: Unified API Index

title: How unified APIs handle webhooks, rate limits, OAuth, and pagination
description: A feature-by-feature evidence map for Bindbee, Merge, and Unified.to, with unsupported behavior kept explicit.
summary: Treat webhooks, quota, OAuth, and pagination as four independent state machines because unified APIs normalize each one to different depths.
author: Unified API Index

title: Which unified APIs publicly verify SOC 2, HIPAA, and ISO 27001?
description: A dated distinction between public compliance claims, trust-portal listings, current artifacts, and unsupported in-progress labels.
summary: Merge publicly lists all three controls in its trust center; Bindbee publicly claims all three, while Finch and Unified.to do not publicly establish ISO 27001 in the reviewed evidence.
author: Unified API Index

title: Why Manual Benefits CSV Uploads Cause Data Errors and Onboarding Delays
description: A guide to the error paths, setup work, freshness limits, and evaluation criteria behind manual CSV workflows in benefits software.
summary: Manual benefits CSV uploads fail when repeated human handoffs, provider-specific schemas, batch timing, and correction cycles are treated as a reliable data pipeline.
author: Unified API Index

title: Workday RaaS, SOAP, and REST: what can a unified API abstract?
description: A technical boundary map for Workday Reports-as-a-Service, SOAP, REST, tenant setup, security, schema mapping, and unified APIs.
summary: The reviewed evidence supports a narrow Workday boundary. A unified layer can map selected source fields into its normalized model, while Workday still exposes tenant-owned surfaces and permissions. Workday publishes an official SOAP reference; Unified.to describes SOAP, REST, and RaaS roles; public Bindbee evidence reviewed here establishes custom-field mapping, not full Workday surface support.
author: Unified API Index
